track.why: Logged route is 'East Ridge', report describes leaving the Jerry Lakes camp, dropping ~800 ft into the next basin, climbing the SE arm, gaining the East Ridge at ~7,200 ft with three 5th-class steps, summit, same line down. Track ends at the summit (7 m). BUT it is a camp-to-summit-to-camp day (starts at the Jerry Lakes basin ~48.757,-120.923), not trailhead-to-summit and not a full round trip from a road; the route has no Trailhead pin to measure from. Owner/apply script decides whether a camp-based round trip qualifies.

facts.text: Despite the Class 4 rating, July parties climbed about three roped-quality fifth-class steps: an early gully, an exposed low-fifth crux mid-ridge, and a pitch near the top.
In mid-July a snow finger near the glacier toe collapsed onto the rock; keep away from thin snow remnants at the toe.
In July, from the Jerry Lakes camp a goat path leads to the col; lose about 800 ft into the next basin, climb the southeast arm, cross a snowfield and scramble to the ridge near 7,200 ft.
Rope, a few cams and slings for the ridge's fifth-class steps (July)
Sandals or camp shoes for the Canyon Creek ford (July)
In July the crux was downclimbed on a protected system and only one rappel off an existing tat anchor was needed lower on the ridge; the glacier basin below was best crossed on snow.

Round trip from the trailhead.

facts.text: About four pickets and a 60 m rope to simul-climb the headwall (May-early June)
In late May, fresh storm snow lay over an icy crust on the headwall, so parties placed pickets and lowered the steepest part on a buried deadman anchor.
In late May, boots and crampons were enough on the snow below the glacier; one party carried snowshoes the whole way and never used them.

facts.text: In July, take the lake boat to the Devils Creek landing and walk about two miles of shoreline to the Devils Creek bridge; fill up there, then climb the game trail just south of the bridge. The next water is a tarn near 5,700 ft (a pool on point 6,486 early in the month).

A second July party camped on flat slabs at the glacier base near 5,400 ft after about 5.5 hours; cliff bands near 3,400 ft needed a few mossy class 4 moves and the timber above 5,000 ft turned brushy, and tracks from the snow-season headwall route do not help because snow hid the worst brush.
The fractured notch on the ridge is loose and exposed; one July party retreated there, another bypassed it on a loose talus traverse to where the glacier meets the ridge.
In July the last few hundred feet of the ridge carry icy patches, and the gullies after the first saddle are very loose, so spread the party out.
Early on, the black pinnacle (point 6,937 ft) is a straightforward class 3 scramble, but the downclimb beyond it is loose enough to turn partners back.
